audit.whatIsWrong: content.early opens "Kennen has no blind and no dash" and whys[0] repeats "no blind, no dash, no sustain". Kennen has Lightning Rush — a 10/9/8/7/6s form change that passes through units, grants Move Speed on entry and Attack Speed on exit, and applies a Mark of the Storm as it passes. The full layer of this same page calls Lightning Rush "his escape" and builds its whole commit rule around it. The two layers contradict each other.
audit.why: This is the ability that decides whether a Jayce all-in connects. Lightning Rush passes through the minion wave, so it both closes the gap Thundering Blow is supposed to open and leaves him with attack speed for the Electrical Surge follow-up. Telling the reader Kennen has no dash is telling him his knockback is a full answer when it is half of one — and it means he commits on a cooldown that is already up.
audit.corrected: Lightning Rush named with its 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown, the unit-pass, the Move Speed in and Attack Speed out, and the mark it applies. Commit rule tied to it being spent.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (E Lightning Rush: CD 10/9/8/7/6, 'morphs into a lightning form, enabling him to pass through units and apply a Mark of the Storm... gains Move Speed when entering this form, and attack speed when leaving it')

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] calls Slicing Maelstrom a "channeled AoE", and no cooldown appears anywhere on the page despite mid saying "only commit when his ult is down".
audit.why: Riot's text for Slicing Maelstrom is "summons a storm that strikes at nearby enemy champions for magical damage" — nothing about a channel, and the kit's derived flags list only zone, not channel. Calling it a channel invites a reader to try to interrupt it with Thundering Blow, which wastes a 20s knockback for nothing. The cooldown is a flat 120s, which is the number that makes "commit when his ult is down" actionable: two minutes is an entire wave cycle of free poke.
audit.corrected: "Channeled" removed; the flat 120s cooldown written into the level-6 spike and the mid block, alongside Thundering Shuriken at 7s rank 1 and Electrical Surge at 13s rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (R Slicing Maelstrom: CD 120, range 550, flags: zone only; Q CD 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4; W CD 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6)

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart reads Jayce, Skill, Kennen, Kennen, Jayce, Kennen, Kennen — it gives Kennen levels 3, 4-5 and first item, then gives Jayce level 6 back. Every one of those four stages contradicts the page's own prose: whys[2] says the gate-Q means "I poke his last-hits all day", whys[3] says "the poke war keeps tilting my way", whys[5] calls first item "my Eclipse/Manamune spike", and whys[4] says level 6 is where "a 3-stack Mark of the Storm stun can flip a trade".
audit.why: The chart is inverted at four of seven stages, and the matchup wins 53.37% for Jayce. A reader who trusts the chart plays passively through his three strongest levels and then dives into the one ability the prose tells him to fear.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3, 4-5 and first item to Jayce, Level 6 to Skill, 2+ items left with Kennen — Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Jayce, Kennen.
sources: content whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], whys[5], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page explains why Electrical Surge hurts more than its damage number suggests.
audit.why: Electrical Surge is on-hit: it passively adds damage and a Mark of the Storm every few attacks, and Lightning Rush hands him attack speed on exit. That chain means his damage scales with attack speed, so armour alone reads the trade wrong — and it also means the third mark can arrive from an auto rather than a spell, which is the stun a reader watching only Q and R will never see coming.
audit.corrected: Electrical Surge named as the on-hit mark source, with the Lightning Rush attack-speed hand-off that feeds it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (W Electrical Surge: onHit, 'passively deals extra damage and adds a Mark of the Storm to his target every few attacks')

notes: FACTUAL ERROR: content.early and whys[0] both assert Kennen has "no dash". Lightning Rush is a 10/9/8/7/6s form change that passes through units, gives Move Speed on entry and Attack Speed on exit, and applies a Mark of the Storm on the way past — and the FULL layer of this same matchup names it as the tracked ability and builds the commit rule on it. The two layers were carrying opposite beliefs about whether Kennen can close a gap. Second error: spikes[2] calls Slicing Maelstrom "channeled". Riot's text says only that it summons a storm striking nearby enemy champions, and the kit's flags list zone with no channel flag — a reader who believes it is a channel will spend a 20s Thundering Blow trying to interrupt it. Added: Electrical Surge is the on-hit mark source, so the stun's third stack frequently arrives from an auto-attack rather than a spell, which is invisible to a reader tracking only Q and R. Cooldowns added: Slicing Maelstrom 120s flat, Lightning Rush 10/9/8/7/6s, Thundering Shuriken 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4s at 950 range, Electrical Surge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s. LEVEL CHART: four of seven stages contradicted the prose (Kennen given 3, 4-5 and first item; Jayce given 6) in a matchup Jayce wins 53.37%. UNVERIFIED and therefore left alone: whys[0] claimed the gate-Q "out-ranges his Thundering Shuriken". Shock Blast's cannon-form range is not in the kit file (the listed 600 is the hammer leap), so I could not confirm it against Thundering Shuriken's 950 and removed the comparison rather than restate it.
